messages.subject: Compute SE using LDSCoutput$V
parts:
Hi all!

I've been using Genomic SEM to get the genetic correlations between a large number of traits (because it's much more convenient than using LDSC). I've derived the SE for the genetic correlation using: 

k<-nrow(LDSCoutput$S)
SE<-matrix(0, k, k
SE[lower.tri(SE,diag=TRUE)] <-sqrt(diag(LDSCoutput$V))

However, the results I get are not the same as what is printed in the log file. At least, I think the SE is here:

Genetic Correlation between x and y: 0.9249 (0.0322)

Is that right? Does anyone know what else might be going on?

messages.author: 424edea90949f8a3
messages.subject: Re: Compute SE using LDSCoutput$V
parts:
Just in case anyone else wants to get the SE from LDSC output (in gsem_obj), here's a function (adapted from the function used to report SE in the logfile, credits to my colleague Jacob Bergstedt):

compute_SE_of_rg <- function(gsem_obj) {
 
  S <- gsem_obj$S
  V <- gsem_obj$V
 
  ratio <- tcrossprod(1 / sqrt(diag(S)))
  S_Stand <- S * ratio
 
  scaleO <- gdata::lowerTriangle(ratio, diag = TRUE)

  #rescale the sampling correlation matrix by the appropriate diagonals
  V_Stand <- V * tcrossprod(scaleO)
 
  #enter SEs from diagonal of standardized V
  r <- nrow(S)
  SE_Stand <- matrix(0, r, r)
  SE_Stand[lower.tri(SE_Stand, diag = TRUE)] <- sqrt(diag(V_Stand))
  as.data.frame(as.matrix(Matrix::forceSymmetric(SE_Stand, "L")))

}
